questionText:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be any two invertible matrices of the same order. Match List-I with List-II:
List-I:
(A) $(PQ)^{-1}$
(B) $(P^{-1}Q)^{-1}$
(C) $(PQ^{-1})^{-1}$
(D) $(P^{-1}Q^{-1})^{-1}$

List-II:
(I) $Q^{-1}P$
(II) $QP^{-1}$
(III) $Q^{-1}P^{-1}$
(IV) $QP$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below[cite: 3]:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Using the reversal law for matrix inverses $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$ and the identity $(M^{-1})^{-1} = M$:
1. $(PQ)^{-1} = Q^{-1}P^{-1} \implies$ (A) matches (III)[cite: 3].
2. $(P^{-1}Q)^{-1} = Q^{-1}(P^{-1})^{-1} = Q^{-1}P \implies$ (B) matches (I)[cite: 3].
3. $(PQ^{-1})^{-1} = (Q^{-1})^{-1}P^{-1} = QP^{-1} \implies$ (C) matches (II)[cite: 3].
4. $(P^{-1}Q^{-1})^{-1} = (Q^{-1})^{-1}(P^{-1})^{-1} = QP \implies$ (D) matches (IV)[cite: 3].
Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)[cite: 3].
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.

2. $(P^{-1}Q)^{-1} = Q^{-1}(P^{-1})^{-1} = Q^{-1}P \implies$ (B) matches (I)[cite: 3].
3. $(PQ^{-1})^{-1} = (Q^{-1})^{-1}P^{-1} = QP^{-1} \implies$ (C) matches (II)[cite: 3].
4. $(P^{-1}Q^{-1})^{-1} = (Q^{-1})^{-1}(P^{-1})^{-1} = QP \implies$ (D) matches (IV)[cite: 3].
Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)[cite: 3].
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.
